rationale:
The 2026-10-03 VERIFICATION round for analyzer/HASKELL. Its predecessor round fixed the QUOTES on an FFI entity but recorded the header case as unreachable, from a count of entity NODES; the header is inside the same string literal, so no node census can see it. Re-probing the corpus produced four findings, three defects and one GAP, and this fixture pins all four plus the controls that say the fixes did not over-reach.

(1) FFI HEADER. Over the 1,356 quoted FFI literals GHC writes, 391 carry a HEADER AND THE C NAME IN ONE STRING and the analyzer published the header as the symbol: `references log1pDoubleOld -> "math.h log1p"` (testsuite/tests/codeGen/should_run/cgrun078.hs:21), `references functionInC -> "T15933.h function_in_c"` (testsuite/tests/ffi/should_run/T15933.hs:8). Haskell 2010 Report F.3.2.1 `impent -> 'static' [chname] [&] [cid] | string`: in the string form the header and the entity share one literal, so the entity is the LAST whitespace-separated token.

(2) FFI `&`. 42 of those literals are `&`-prefixed — Report F.3.2.1's `[&]`, meaning pass-the-address-of, not part of the spelling. `references ghc_unique_counter64 -> "&ghc_unique_counter64"` at compiler/GHC/Types/Unique/Supply.hs:280.

(3) FFI `javascript`. Over a stride-12 draw of the corpus (1,170 files, 62 `foreign_import` nodes, script/m14/tmp/hs-verify-ffi-conv.ts) 13 of 13 `javascript` nodes bind a JAVASCRIPT BODY and not one names an entity — yet 8 SHIPPED as `references` edges, because a JS snippet contains none of the characters pool-worker.filterNoiseRelationships bans: `references js_print -> "console.log($1)"`, `references js_req_to_str -> "$1.text($2)"` (testsuite/tests/jsffi/http.hs:18-45). Under rule R7 the honest state for no-entity-named is ABSENCE, so no `references` edge is published while the declaration still publishes its symbol and its `contains` edge.

(4) QUALIFIED INSTANCE TARGET — a GAP in the workstream's sense (the language HAS the construct and the analyzer was not reading it). `instance TrieMap IntMap.IntMap` parses as `type_patterns -> qualified("IntMap.IntMap")`; no branch of processInstance matched, `targetType` stayed empty, and the instance SYMBOL was published under the CLASS's own name — a second symbol named `TrieMap` beside the file's own `class TrieMap` — while `implements IntMap.IntMap -> TrieMap`, an edge the language plainly expresses, was never emitted. Corpus: compiler/GHC/Data/TrieMap.hs:139, compiler/GHC/Types/Unique/DSM.hs:158.

The controls matter as much as the pins. `widget_alloc`, `wrapper`, `dynamic` and `widget_version` are name-only literals on C conventions and must be published UNCHANGED, so a mutant that made foreignEntityName return the wrong thing, return nothing, or apply the javascript branch to every convention would each break a pin rather than pass by accident. `instance Surface Widget` and `instance Surface [Int]` are the unqualified targets, pinned so the qualified branch cannot pass by naming something.

A regression the fix itself introduced, and the guard for it: adding "qualified" to processInstance's type-SCANNING list let a later type pattern of a MULTI-PARAMETER instance hijack the target, moving 2 `implements` and 5 `overrides` edges onto the wrong type (compiler/GHC/HsToCore/Quote.hs:1239 `instance RepTV (HsBndrVis GhcRn) TH.BndrVis`, type_patterns [0]=parens [1]=qualified; compiler/GHC/ThToHs.hs:1600). The shipped rule reads POSITION — a `qualified` first pattern — which is strictly additive: every shape the pre-existing branches read is still read by them. `Convertible` below pins the multi-parameter case in both directions, and `haskell/instance-qualified-hijacks-multiparam` is the mutant.

This forbid also catches the naive fix that applies the last-token rule to every convention, which would publish `}` instead.
the naive last-token-everywhere fix, stated separately because it is a DIFFERENT wrong answer and a pin that forbade only the full literal would miss it
the FIX 3 pre-state in edge form: the instance was named after the class. A self-implements row is the shape that state produces whenever the class and the unnamed target coincide.
the FFI entity is an EXTERNAL symbol and must never be claimed as contained by this module — the `contains` half of FIX 1 that a mutant turning the entity into a symbol would produce

the exact hijack the type-scan produced on `instance Convertible (Maybe Widget) Store.Map`: a LATER qualified pattern must not become the target. This is the corpus shape — compiler/GHC/HsToCore/Quote.hs:1239 — so the fixture reproduces the defect rather than a nearby one.
